neighbours.label: the 't of can't / couldn't in an exclamation of being emotionally overwhelmed (I can't believe..., I couldn't help it, can't wait), not can't for practical inability
neighbours.notes: Card: peak tokens 't / ’t of can't; output suppresses disbelief, shock, stunned, astonished. Probes: 'I won the lottery. I can't believe it' 1.16, 'the printer can't print in color' 0.02. 'I am in total shock' (no can't) 0.32, so some meaning carries without the word; label is kept at the can't-in-context level.
fire: We just found out we're having twins. I can't believe it!
My brother survived the crash without a scratch. I still can't believe it.
The ending of that movie wrecked me, I can't handle it.
When they called my name on stage I couldn't stop crying.
Our first trip to Japan is next week and I can't wait!
He looked so silly in that hat that I couldn't help laughing.
She read my letter and said, "I can't believe you remembered."
After all these years at home, I honestly can't believe I'm leaving.
quiet: We just found out the clinic is closed, so we can't book a scan today.
My brother's car has a flat tire, so he can't drive to work.
The file on that disk is corrupted, so the player can't open it.
When they called my name the microphone couldn't pick up my voice.
Our first trip to Japan is next week but we can't take the dog.
He wore such a big hat that he couldn't fit through the door.
She read my letter and said, "I can't read your handwriting here."
After all these years at home, I still can't find the spare key.
